novelty.justification: The claim’s novel route is the predicted relationship that the repetition-induced endorsement lift is “largely NOT gated by the attributed source’s credibility,” supplemented by the mechanism that familiarity and credibility signals are “separately decodable and only weakly coupled at the verdict.” Searches using “LLM illusory truth effect repetition source credibility,” “language model repetition source reliability endorsement,” and “mechanistic sycophancy user expertise authority activation patching” identify the closest work as Susceptibility to Influence of Large Language Models (2023), which already reports an LLM illusory-truth effect, and When Truth Is Overridden (2025), which reports negligible effects of user-expertise framing and mechanistically studies factual override. Crossing established LLM repetition effects with source credibility is therefore a natural but non-trivial extension rather than a wholly new phenomenon; the explicit repetition-by-credibility interaction and separable-but-uncoupled internal-signal hypothesis add substantive operationalization, but the probing, patching, and steering methods are standard rather than a new measurement paradigm.
